'''Kenneth Meade Lakin''' (January 14, 1941 – November 24, 2012) was an American physicist and engineer known for pioneering work on thin-film acoustic resonators. He is widely credited with inventing and developing the [[solidly mounted resonator]] (SMR) and advancing the thin-film bulk acoustic resonator (TFBAR) technology used in microwave filters for mobile and wireless communications.<ref name=UFFCmem>{{cite web |title=Kenneth Meade Lakin |url=https://ieee-uffc.org/about/in-memoria?page=4
 |website=IEEE Ultrasonics, Ferroelectrics, and Frequency Control Society |date=November 30, 2016 |access-date=6 September 2025}}</ref><ref name=Redmond>{{cite web |title=Kenneth Meade Lakin Obituary |url=https://www.redmondmemorial.com/m/obituaries/Kenneth-Lakin/
 |website=Autumn Funerals (Redmond, OR) |access-date=6 September 2025}}</ref>

==Biography==
Lakin was born in Grand Rapids, Michigan, to Mabel (Meade) and Harold Lakin, and grew up in Portland, Michigan.<ref name=UFFCmem/> He earned B.S. and M.S. degrees in physics, mathematics, and electrical engineering from the [[University of Michigan]], and a Ph.D. in applied physics from [[Stanford University]] in 1969.<ref name=UFFCmem/> He died at home near Redmond, Oregon, on November 24, 2012, following an extended illness.<ref name=UFFCmem/><ref name=Legacy>{{cite web |title=Kenneth Meade Lakin Obituary (2012) |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/lsj/name/kenneth-lakin-obituary?id=8327147
 |website=Legacy.com |date=December 2, 2012 |access-date=6 September 2025}}</ref>

==Career==
From 1969 to 1980, Lakin was on the faculty of the [[University of Southern California]], conducting research on surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices, thin-film resonators, and piezoelectric film growth and characterization.<ref name=UFFCmem/> In 1980 he joined [[Ames National Laboratory|Ames Laboratory]]/[[Iowa State University]], where he founded the Microelectronics Research Center (MRC) and served there until 1989.<ref name=UFFCmem/>

In 1989, Lakin founded '''TFR Technologies, Inc.''' in Oregon, serving as president and CEO. Under his leadership the company advanced thin-film resonator devices and filters, and participated in multiple U.S. [[Small Business Innovation Research|SBIR]] programs related to thin-film resonator microwave-acoustic filters.<ref>{{cite web |title=THIN FILM RESONATOR MICROWAVE-ACOUSTIC FILTERS (SBIR Award, 1992) |url=https://www.sbir.gov/awards/116359
 |website=SBIR.gov |access-date=6 September 2025}}</ref> He retired from TFR Technologies in 2005.<ref name=Legacy/>

==Research and legacy==
Lakin's work established the practical SMR structure—depositing a piezoelectric thin film on an acoustic Bragg reflector to confine energy and enable high-frequency operation on generic substrates—leading to compact, manufacturable BAW filters for RF front ends. He authored more than 100 technical publications and was granted at least 21 U.S. patents covering resonators, filters, and fabrication methods.<ref name=Legacy/><ref>{{cite web |title=Kenneth M. Lakin – Inventions, Patents and Patent Applications |url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/kenneth-m-lakin
 |website=Justia Patents |access-date=6 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Patents assigned to TFR Technologies, Inc. |url=https://patents.justia.com/assignee/tfr-technologies-inc
 |website=Justia Patents |access-date=6 September 2025}}</ref>

His 2005 review article in ''IEEE Transactions on Ultrasonics, Ferroelectrics, and Frequency Control'' summarized thin-film resonator technology and influenced academic and industrial development of BAW filters used in mobile phones and wireless infrastructure.<ref name="Lakin 2005 707–716">{{cite journal |last=Lakin |first=Kenneth M. |title=Thin film resonator technology |journal=IEEE Transactions on Ultrasonics, Ferroelectrics, and Frequency Control |volume=52 |issue=5 |pages=707–716 |year=2005 |doi=10.1109/TUFFC.2005.1503959 |pmid=16048174 |bibcode=2005ITUFF..52..707L }}</ref>

==Awards and honors==

'''Walter G. Cady Award''' (2003), [[IEEE Ultrasonics, Ferroelectrics, and Frequency Control Society]]—for “outstanding and innovative work leading to the development of miniature, thin film resonator filters in commercially viable products.”<ref>{{cite web |title=Walter G. Cady Award – 2003 Recipient: Kenneth Lakin |url=https://ieee-uffc.org/award/walter-g-cady-award
 |website=IEEE UFFC |access-date=6 September 2025}}</ref>

'''IEEE Fellow''' (effective January 1, 2004), “for contributions to thin-film resonator technology and applications.”<ref>{{cite web |title=UFFC-S Newsletter, Number 38 (Spring 2005): 2004 IEEE Fellow Recipient Kenneth Meade Lakin |url=https://ieee-uffc.org/files/ieeeuffcorg/2023-11/UFFC-S%20Newsletter%20Spring%202005.pdf
 |website=IEEE UFFC |access-date=6 September 2025}}</ref>

'''IEEE UFFC Society Achievement Award''' (2010), recognizing pioneering contributions to AlN-based BAW/SMR devices and filters.<ref name=UFFCmem/>
